# session_login_cached — POST /login → cached token reused on drain 2.
# Verifies the runner honours requests[].cache: drain 1 captures the
# response's session_token into state.session_token + the paired expiry
# stamp at state.session_token_expires_at; drain 2 reads the cached value
# within its expiry_buffer and SKIPS the /login step entirely (only /events
# is traced). The spec is loaded live from the embedded template.

exec skopos template show -o spec.yml session_login_cached
replace spec.yml http://localhost:9999 $URL

# Drain 1: cold cache. Both /login (cache miss → fetch) and /events traced.
exec skopos run -i spec.yml --once --state state.json --trace trace1.jsonl --out events1.jsonl
normalize trace1.jsonl
cmp trace1.jsonl want_trace1.jsonl
cmp events1.jsonl want_events1.jsonl

# Drain 1 captured the issued token into state.session_token and paired it
# with an expiry stamp at state.session_token_expires_at.
grep '"session_token": "session-token-0001"' state.json
grep 'session_token_expires_at' state.json

# Drain 2: warm cache. /login MUST NOT appear in the trace — only /events.
exec skopos run -i spec.yml --once --state state.json --trace trace2.jsonl --out events2.jsonl
normalize trace2.jsonl
cmp trace2.jsonl want_trace2.jsonl
cmp events2.jsonl want_events2.jsonl

# Cached token was reused, NOT re-issued — the testserver's login counter
# never advanced past 0001, so state.session_token stays "session-token-0001".
grep '"session_token": "session-token-0001"' state.json
! grep 'session-token-0002' state.json

-- want_trace1.jsonl --
